blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Blood Relations is a key topic covered under Section 6 of SSC Reasoning.
Family relations are categorized and studied using dedicated reference tables.
Syllogism problems in Section 7 rely primarily on the basic Venn Diagram Method.

Concept:

Blood relation questions test the ability to understand family relationships based on given information.

blocks.content:
In SSC, blood relation questions are:

• Direct

• Mostly one family at a time

• No complex puzzles

Method to Solve:

1. Identify the starting person

2. Move step-by-step

3. Draw a simple family tree if needed

4. Read the question carefully till the end

Solved Examples:



Example 1:

A is the father of B. B is the sister of C.

How is A related to C?

Logic:

A → father of B

B → sister of C

So A is also father of C

Answer: Father

Example 2:

P is the brother of Q. Q is the mother of R.

How is P related to R?

Logic:

P → brother of mother

So P is maternal uncle

Answer: Uncle

Practice Questions (Blood Relations):

Q1. A is the son of B. B is the sister of C.

How is C related to A?

A. Uncle

B. Aunt

C. Father

D. Mother



Q2. X is the father of Y. Y is the brother of Z.

How is X related to Z?

A. Father

B. Uncle

C. Brother

D. Grandfather



Q3. P is the sister of Q. Q is the father of R.

How is P related to R?

A. Mother

B. Aunt

C. Sister

D. Grandmother

items: Blood Relations questions regularly test direct and indirect family connections.
Syllogism questions are best solved using Venn Diagram visual overlays to avoid logical fallacies.

blocks.content:
Concept:

Syllogism tests the ability to draw logical conclusions from given statements.



In SSC, syllogism questions are:

• Basic

• Mostly definite conclusions

• Best solved using Venn diagrams



Standard Statements:

1)All A are B

2)Some A are B

3)No A is B
